title: Brand-adaptive glass layering and semi-opaque component overrides for themed console
creator: Marina Alvarez
description: Introduce a brand-adaptive "glass" surface layer and a set of semi-opaque component overrides that allow customer brand colors to harmonize with the console theme without breaking accessibility or telemetry. This work defines token blending rules, fallback semantics for high-contrast and low-contrast brand palettes, and component-level visual overrides for buttons, tables, and charts. Goal: enable customers to apply brand tints (logo/primary) across the console while preserving legibility, chart color readability, and interaction affordances across light, dim, and night themes.
acceptance_criteria: Design tokens defined: glass-surface-{level} tokens for three opacity levels with computed RGB + alpha and recommended use cases
Token mapping matrix submitted for light/dim/night themes and for three brand saturation classes (neutral, saturated, high-contrast)
Button component override spec: primary/ghost/cta variants with minimum 4.5:1 contrast against their immediate background in all themes
Table row and header overrides: background bleed rules and zebra stripe spec that maintain focus outlines and row-hover contrast
Chart color harmonization rules: palette generation algorithm notes and fallback to semantic palettes when brand palette fails contrast thresholds
Figma spec and token JSON uploaded to design tokens repo; engineering PR referencing runtime mapping hook opened
Accessibility sign-off from A11y lead and results of automated contrast checks attached
Performance guardrails documented: token calc complexity limited; runtime mapping must be cacheable and map to precompiled token sets
comments: 2026-02-14 Marina Alvarez: Triage meeting notes — PM wants brand theming to feel 'integrated' but not overpower the console UI or metrics visuals. We scoped a glass layer approach to provide subtle tinting without full-surface recolor.

2026-02-20 Jonah Patel: Initial explorations uploaded to Figma. Three approaches: (A) uniform tint overlay, (B) selective component tinting, (C) blended glass surfaces + selective overrides. We recommend C for flexibility.
2026-02-24 PM review (Sofia Kim): Prefer flexible approach; ask to prioritize charts and tables because customers reported brand themes breaking dashboards in alpha tests.

2026-02-28 Design review feedback (Lead Designer Aaron Lee): Update token naming to follow tokens/surface/glass-{level} pattern, include semantic tokens for chart accents (semantic-positive, semantic-neutral, semantic-negative). Also include explicit fallback to neutral palette for low-contrast brand colors.

2026-03-03 Engineering sync (Eng owner Priya Shah): Noted constraints — runtime mapping must avoid per-render color math to keep render path fast. We'll implement a preflight mapper that picks from a finite set of compiled token variants. ENG-78412 created to track runtime work.

2026-03-06 Jonah Patel: Uploaded final token matrix to Drive (link) and added color ramp generator script notes. Figma frames: https://www.figma.com/file/EXAMPLE/brand-glass-theming, Confluence PRD: https://confluence.redwood/brand-glass-theming

2026-03-09 QA (A11y) automated checks: all button variants pass 4.5:1 against immediate backgrounds in light/dim; night theme requires one exception where saturated brand color needs forced desaturation — documented as fallback rule.

2026-03-10 Marina Alvarez: Preparing reviewer checklist. Engineering PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/12891 — runtime mapping hook and token JSON import. Please review tokens and component override API surface.
2026-03-10 Jonah Patel: Next steps — finalize chart palette generator, add unit tests for token mapper, and schedule a demo with two customer-facing dashboards for validation week of 2026-03-15.
